rulings.evidence: The table's DIFFERENT FORM flag is a plural, breasts against breast, not a form flip. Board-proven at 7 of 7 stores and the food-macros-db row already exists under this exact canon name.

The existing Mozzarella Cheese food-DB row IS the shredded low-moisture part-skim form and its note cites a priced 8 oz bag package row, so this is a reuse, not a new id. Preferred over the generic shredded-cheese blend the table matched; if mozzarella-cheese turns out not to be carried, shredded-cheese (7 of 7, same price class) is the safe fallback.

REJECTED the table's shredded-cheese match on price class: generic bagged mozzarella/cheddar blend runs about a quarter of parmesan per ounce. Parmesan Cheese is an existing vocabulary row and an existing food-DB row (Great Value label), so parmesan is a reuse.
Exact vocabulary row, same form, board-proven at 7 of 7 stores.

A Lawrys-style blend of salt, sugar, paprika, turmeric, onion and garlic, not table salt: about 3 dollars for 8 oz against 1 dollar for 26 oz, a different price class. Refused the salt bridge; pantry-static pricing on 7.5 g is safe and the term is enqueued.

Bare pepper on a flour dredge beside seasoned salt is ground black pepper; the bell-pepper rows the matcher offered are noise. black-pepper is live - the sibling recipe in this same batch carries it as a settled line.

REJECTED the board's french-bread match: a bakery loaf is not dry crumbs. Mapped to the generic dry-crumb row rather than Panko Breadcrumbs, which the food DB deliberately keeps separate at a different density, and the gram weight is stated directly so no panko density is used.

macro_cross_check.verdict: GAP IS REAL AND IT IS NOT A PORTION ERROR. The source's own figures cannot be reconciled with its own ingredient list: 2 1/2 cups of shredded mozzarella alone is 280 g, 851 cal and 66 g protein for 4 servings, which is 213 cal and 16.5 g protein per serving before any chicken. Adding a 200 g breast per serving lands protein at 75 g, so 50 g is unreachable unless the cheese was counted at roughly one third. Halving the chicken to a 100 g breast would still leave protein at 53 g and calories at 780, so no plausible chicken each-weight closes the gap.
macro_cross_check.band_warning: RECOMMEND RETIRE OR RE-BAND. At full purchased basis this is 895 cal and 47 g carbs per serving against the run's 400-650 cal and 35 g carb conditions - it fails both. Sensitivity: dredging discards roughly 40% of the flour, egg and crumb; discounting that fraction gives 818 cal and 34.7 g carbs, so carbs could just squeak under 35 but calories miss the ceiling by 170 under every basis I can construct. This recipe entered the pool on a published figure that its own ingredients do not support.
macro_cross_check.uncertainty: The chicken each-weight (200 g) is my assumption and the highest-cost one here, but it is not what breaks the band - cheese and breading are.
